content: If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is important to follow their instructions carefully. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure that you have been thoroughly trained by your healthcare provider on how to prepare and use it. Before using the medication, inspect it visually for any particles or discoloration. If you notice either, do not use the liquid. For optimal effectiveness, administer this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the entire prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication prematurely may result in a return of the infection. Common side effects of this medication may include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, blurred vision, or redness, discomfort, pain, or swelling at the injection site. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, this medication may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush, a new vaginal yeast infection (fungal infections), or a new type of bacterial infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek immediate medical attention. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using aztreonam, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, or to penicillins, cephalosporins, or other antibiotics such as imipenem or meropenem, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may rarely cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Aztreonam may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as some diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, your doctor may order lab or medical tests to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not double doses to catch up. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
